---
title: "sblr Notes"
---

These notes describe the statistical models, data representations, sparse-LD
workflows, annotation-informed priors, and technical details behind `sblr`.
They are organized as a readable main path supported by practical workflow
notes and more detailed technical appendices.

`sblr` is an experimental research package. The notes distinguish current
public workflows from lower-level or research-stage model components and
identify the assumptions needed to interpret their outputs.

## Recommended Reading Order

New readers can follow this sequence:

1. [Model Overview](model_overview.html) for the package landscape and model
   selection map.
2. [ST-BLR Interface and Output Map](stblr_interface_and_output_map.html) for
   the current `stblr_csr()`, `stblr_bed()`, and `stblr_csr_annot()`
   interfaces, shared `Glist` object, standardized outputs, helpers, and
   unsupported combinations.
3. [Data Representations](data_representations.html) for the relationship
   between individual-level data and summary statistics plus LD.
4. [Single-Trait Models](single_trait_models.html) for the core sparse BLR
   model used by the current BED and CSR workflows.
5. [Sparse-LD and BED Workflows](sparse_ld_and_bed_workflows.html) for the
   practical path from PLINK BED data to sufficient statistics and disk-backed
   CSR LD.
6. [Annotation-Informed Models](annotation_informed_models.html) for fixed,
   learned, group, and SBayesRC-style annotation priors.
7. [selection_s Implementation Status](selection_s_status.md) for the current
   fixed global and sampled trait-specific BayesS-style MAF-scaling support.
8. [Workflows and Outputs](workflows_and_outputs.html) for running the main
   workflows and interpreting returned fit objects.
9. [Multi-Trait Models](multi_trait_models.html) for joint trait-sharing and
   covariance models.
10. Consult the [technical appendices](#technical-appendices) as needed for
   derivations, implementation contracts, and detailed assumptions.

## Main Explanatory Notes

- [Model Overview](model_overview.html) maps the main package axes:
  single-trait versus multi-trait, individual-level versus summary-statistics,
  and plain versus annotation-informed priors.

- [ST-BLR Interface and Output Map](stblr_interface_and_output_map.html)
  maps `stblr_csr()`, `stblr_bed()`, and `stblr_csr_annot()`, the shared
  `Glist` object, summary-statistics and sparse-LD preparation, current
  model-family support, standardized outputs, helper functions, and
  fine-mapping diagnostics.

- [Data Representations](data_representations.html) explains individual-level
  genotype and phenotype inputs, sufficient statistics, LD, CSR storage, and
  marker-order alignment.

- [Single-Trait Models](single_trait_models.html) defines the core ST-BLR
  model, BayesC-style sparse prior, BED and CSR fitting paths, scheduled sparse
  updates, and posterior outputs.

- [Multi-Trait Models](multi_trait_models.html) introduces joint MT-BLR,
  trait-sharing patterns, genetic and residual covariance, sample-overlap
  requirements, and the current implementation status.

- [Annotation-Informed Models](annotation_informed_models.html) compares
  fixed marker-specific priors, learned annotation effects, group priors, and
  the SBayesRC-style annotation-dependent BayesR prior.

- [selection_s Implementation Status](selection_s_status.md) summarizes the
  current fixed global and sampled trait-specific `selection_s` support matrix,
  scale convention, defaults, and BayesR/SBayesRC component naming.

## Practical Workflow Notes

- [Sparse-LD and BED Workflows](sparse_ld_and_bed_workflows.html) is the
  practical guide to aligning BED markers, deriving sufficient statistics,
  constructing sparse LD with `make_sparse_ld()`, fitting `stblr_csr()`, and
  cautiously comparing BED and CSR fits.

- [Workflows and Outputs](workflows_and_outputs.html) connects the executable
  workflow scripts to fit-object components, compact summaries, diagnostics,
  interpretation, and recommended reporting.

The workflow scripts are runnable demonstrations and validation templates,
not automatically lightweight package examples. Production analyses require
appropriate MCMC settings, convergence checks, and sensitivity analyses.

## Technical Appendices

- [Summary Statistics](technical_summary_statistics.html) derives the
  cross-product representation used by single- and multi-trait BLR and
  explains equivalence assumptions and practical limitations.

- [Sparse LD and CSR](technical_sparse_ld_csr.html) defines compressed sparse
  row storage, the disk-backed LD contract, indexing and diagonal conventions,
  construction settings, and validation checks.

- [Annotation-Informed Priors](technical_annotation_priors.html) develops
  marker-specific inclusion and variance priors, empirical-Bayes
  constructions, learned effects, group priors, and regularization choices.

- [SBayesRC-Style Annotation Priors](technical_sbayesrc_annotations.html)
  explains the annotation-dependent BayesR mixture prior, probit
  stick-breaking probabilities, alpha updates, diagnostics, and differences
  from published GCTB SBayesRC.

- [Multi-Trait Sample Overlap](technical_multitrait_overlap.html) gives the
  detailed treatment of `SSY`, pairwise sample overlap, covariance
  reconstruction, current implementation constraints, and sensitivity
  analysis.

Some appendices may still be expanded as the package API stabilizes.
